title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
statement: Return the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray of `nums`, where the array is circular. A circular subarray may wrap from the end back to the start. A one-interval ordinary subarray is also allowed.
hints: The answer is either a normal Kadane maximum or the total sum minus a minimum subarray in the middle.
The wrap-around case is invalid when the minimum subarray is the entire array, which happens when every element is negative.
Run max-Kadane and min-Kadane in one pass, then take max(best_max, total - best_min) unless best_max is negative.

approaches.name: Duplicate the array
approaches.explanation: Search every start and a length up to n on nums + nums.

approaches.name: Kadane plus inverted Kadane
approaches.explanation: Max subarray, or total minus min subarray.

editorial: A maximum circular subarray either does not wrap, which is ordinary Kadane, or it wraps. The wrapping case is the total sum minus the minimum non-wrapping subarray that was excluded from the middle. If the maximum element is negative, that exclusion would be the whole array and the wrap sum would be 0, so return the ordinary maximum instead.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def max_subarray_sum_circular(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    total = best_max = cur_max = best_min = cur_min = nums[0]
    for value in nums[1:]:
        total += value
        cur_max = max(value, cur_max + value)
        best_max = max(best_max, cur_max)
        cur_min = min(value, cur_min + value)
        best_min = min(best_min, cur_min)
    if best_max < 0:
        return best_max
    return max(best_max, total - best_min)
